A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DVD-Quant and have readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements. V2 refers to an unavailable supplementary file for derivation details and Wan2.1 configurations/results, limiting those comparisons.

before.justification: V1 reports original HunyuanVideo/VBench evaluations, component ablations, threshold experiments, TeaCache integration, and memory/latency measurements in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and reports new BGR quantization-error measurements across layers in Figure 3.

M1.justification: V1's PBQ searches progressively tightened per-channel bounds. V2's BGR uses bounded search for initialization and adds iterative updates of the quantization scale, zero-point, and quantized weights (Section 3.1; Algorithm 1). This substantially changes the weight-quantization procedure; the ARQ and threshold-switching framework is largely retained.

E1.justification: The documented dataset/task coverage remains VBench video generation with eight quality dimensions. V2 mentions applying the method to Wan2.1, an additional model rather than an established new dataset or task. Its supplementary evaluation details are unavailable.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the BF16 HunyuanVideo reference and MinMax, SmoothQuant, Quarot, and ViDiT-Q comparators. Table 2 retains STP, ITP, ABS, and SBA. The supplied comparisons establish no comparator additions or removals.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes the diagnostic evaluation from selected-layer error distributions and standard deviations to quantization error across layer indices. V2 also reports application to Wan2.1, with configurations deferred to the unavailable supplement. The stated HunyuanVideo protocol remains 50 steps, CFG 6.0, flow shift 7.0, and one RTX4090.

E4.justification: Figure 3 replaces PBQ/ARQ error-distribution diagnostics with BGR-versus-MinMax error profiles across six module families, removing the direct ARQ distribution comparison. The component ablation table relabels PBQ as BGR while retaining its scores; mixed-precision comparisons and threshold-sensitivity evidence otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty on benchmark scores. V1's Figure 3 standard deviations describe elementwise quantization-error distributions, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the qualitative video examples retain their values/content. New Figure 3 reports BGR error reductions of 86.37%–91.54%, using different measurements from v1's reported 39% error-standard-deviation reduction. Section 4.2 changes W4A4 aesthetic/imaging scores from 61.96/61.82 to 58.94/60.38, but Table 1 retains 61.96/61.82, creating conflicting reports rather than an established performance decline.

T1.justification: V2 introduces explicit scale/zero-point optimization, a least-squares scale solution, and sequential refinement equations (Section 3.1, Equations 3–8), substantially extending v1's bound-tightening mathematics. The normalized feature-distance definition also changes its comparison and denominator from F_{t+1} to F_{t-1} in the bit-switching rule.

C1.justification: V2 redefines a central contribution from PBQ bound tightening to BGR grid refinement. Its abstract and conclusion broaden the approximately 2× speedup claim from HunyuanVideo to advanced DiT models. The introduction drops the assertion of theoretical ARQ error bounds, while retaining the data-free W4A4 novelty and visual-quality claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains bounded search as an initialization for subsequent optimization and more explicitly attributes channel-wise consistency to scaling after rotation. Its efficiency discussion explains why alternating W4A4/W4A8 permits standard kernels. Existing calibration limitations and quality-versus-precision tradeoffs largely remain.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 newly documents initialization, refinement loops, and a stopping tolerance. Section 4.4 adds the explanation that mixed W4A6 can use existing W4A4/W4A8 GEMM kernels. Hardware disclosure and the promise of future code/model availability at the same repository remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds OmniQuant as a bounded-search reference and cites Wan for the additional model application. It removes the UViT discussion and its All Are Worth Words citation. The broader positioning against calibration-based PTQ and existing video quantization methods remains similar.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and much experimental prose remain intact. V2 edits the introduction, related work, and method explanations, updates PBQ/BGR terminology and author affiliations, changes citations to author–year style, and swaps the memory/latency and cache-integration subsections.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the weight-method panel in Figure 2, replaces Figure 3's eight distribution plots with six layerwise error plots, and adds a substantial algorithm display. Typography and page layout change throughout, with tables and figures relocated. Figures 1, 4, 5, and 6 retain their underlying visual evidence.

improvement.justification: BGR's explicit optimization equations, pseudocode, and layerwise diagnostics add useful methodological detail. However, Algorithm 1 initializes j=0 before accessing j−1 quantities, and v2 introduces a Section 4.2/Table 1 score conflict. The unavailable supplementary evidence also prevents checking its broader model claims. These benefits and new verification problems prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
